name: Swedish Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Jantunen, Tommi, Johanna Mesch, Anna Puupponen & Jorma Laaksonen. 2016. On the rhythm of head movements in Finnish and Swedish Sign Language sentences. Proc. Speech Prosody 2016, 850–853. doi:10.21437/SpeechProsody.2016-174
sources.note: Computer-vision study of head-movement rhythm relative to clause boundaries in FinSL and SSL; no mention of stress or prominence at the sign level.

sources.citation: Puupponen, Anna, Tommi Jantunen & Johanna Mesch. 2016. The alignment of head nods with syntactic units in Finnish Sign Language and Swedish Sign Language. Proc. Speech Prosody 2016, 168–172. doi:10.21437/SpeechProsody.2016-35
sources.note: Sentence-level prosody only: head nods align with syntactic boundaries; non-boundary nods perform 'functions such as emphasis or affirmation' (p. 170). No statement on word/sign stress.

sources.citation: Ahlgren, Inger & Brita Bergman. 2006. Det svenska teckenspråket. In: Teckenspråk och teckenspråkiga. Kunskaps- och forskningsöversikt (SOU 2006:29), pp. 11–70. Stockholm: Fritzes.
sources.note: Grammar overview in Swedish: 'Teckenstruktur' (manual component: articulator/articulation/place; transcription; mouth movements/oral components) and 'Grammatik' (word classes, sign-formation processes, sentence formation). No prosody or stress section; 'betoning'/'prosodi' never occur in a phonological sense (only 'En del bokstaverade tecken är betonade synonymer till vanliga tecken', about fingerspelled signs). Silent on word/sign stress.

No phonology, prosody or stress section (History, Hand alphabet, Education, Deaf culture only).
